newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks stage rally after recent declines.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks stage rally after recent declines.

text.p: Swiss shares jumped on Monday, with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index closing 2.6 percent on a correction after recent losses.
Position squaring, gains in Swiss bond futures, a firmer tone on Wall Street and a firmer U.S. dollar also boosted Swiss share prices.
The stronger tone could continue but gains were likely to slow, one dealer said. Further developments would also depend on Wall Street.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares ended up 116.5 points, or 2.61 percent, at 4,588.0 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 66.62 points, or 2.35 percent, to 2,903.15.
Chemicals and pharmaceuticals saw impressive gains.

Clariant, whose 1996 results were received favourably by the market on Friday, soared nearly seven percent, ending up 48 francs at 742. One dealer said the stock also seemed attractive compared with competitor Ciba Specialty Chemicals, which rose 3.75 francs to 120. Roche certificates jumped 500 francs to 12,200. Actively-traded Novartis added 39 francs to 1,758.
Alusuisse, Holderbank, Nestle and SBC all posted gains of more than two percent.
Among financials, CS Group rose 5.25 francs to 164 francs.
UBS was up 19 at 1,278. The company released the results of its separate corporate divisions for the first time on Monday.

Swissair soared 56 francs, or 4.56 percent, to 1,285. The group had reported a 1996 net loss of nearly 500 million francs, but analysts pointed out the stock was sought because of the rise in Swissair's operative results.
Temporary employment firm Adia was up 20 francs at 458.
